entries.reason: BACK-COMPAT ALIAS WITH ZERO CALLSITES — no surface, widget or capability is behind it. CapavateWordmark (client/src/components/CapavateLogo.tsx:32-34) has a one-line body: it returns <CapavateLogo className={className || "h-7 w-auto"} />, i.e. it renders the sibling component in the same file with the same default height. Its own doc comment states the reason it exists — "Convenience wrapper for legacy callsites — preserved for backwards compat. Now identical to <CapavateLogo /> because the brand asset already includes the wordmark." Verified there is nothing to reach: `grep -rn CapavateWordmark client/src` returns exactly ONE line, the declaration itself. The mounted component is CapavateLogo, which renders the real brand asset via Vite's asset pipeline, so the wordmark IS on screen everywhere it is supposed to be — through the canonical component, not through this alias. Nothing a user could previously do is unavailable, because rendering this alias and rendering CapavateLogo produce identical output. Retained rather than deleted so that any un-migrated import in a branch or a partner build keeps compiling.

SUPERSEDED BY TWO REACHABLE SURFACES THAT CALL THE SAME ENDPOINT — verified by endpoint, not by name. PaymentSurface's entire job, per its own header, is: POST /api/billing/plan to mint a real Airwallex PaymentIntent, then redirect the browser to the returned hostedPaymentPageUrl. It explicitly does NOT collect a card number, expiry or CVC. The test that matters for a "silent drop" is whether that capability is still reachable, so the endpoint was searched rather than the component: `grep -rn "api/billing/plan" client/src` returns the declaration in PaymentSurface.tsx:62 plus TWO reachable callers — client/src/pages/founder/Settings.tsx:592 (the Billing tab, reachable, mounted via App.tsx:757) and client/src/pages/founder/Subscribe.tsx:313 (routed at App.tsx:667). Both mint the PaymentIntent and follow hostedPaymentPageUrl. So the founder can still buy the plan, on the same server route, with the same gateway. This is consistent with the recorded direction of travel at client/src/App.tsx:250 and :1407, where the standalone subscribe/payment surface is folded into the billing pages. Airwallex integration is untouched: server/paymentStore.ts and the PaymentSurface-backed store tests (server/__tests__/sprint14_stores.test.ts:293) continue to exercise the cent-reconciliation path. NOTE THE SACRED CONSTRAINT: client/src/pages/founder/Billing.tsx is SACRED, so the remaining consolidation of these checkout entry points is not a Wave 41 action.

UNUSED GENERIC UI PRIMITIVE, NOT A PRODUCT SURFACE — nothing a user could do is behind it. ChipSingleSelect (client/src/components/profile/ChipMultiSelect.tsx:78+) is a presentational single-choice variant of the ChipMultiSelect in the same file: it maps `options` to <button> chips and calls onChange with the chosen value. It owns no route, no query, no mutation, no endpoint and no copy of its own — every string it renders comes from the caller's `options`. `grep -rn ChipSingleSelect client/src` returns exactly ONE line, the declaration. So its unreachability cannot hide a lost capability: there is no data it is the only writer of, and no panel only it can open. The used sibling export in the same module, ChipMultiSelect, is reachable, which is why the module loads. Classified as dead code to be REMOVED rather than as a defect to be mounted — mounting it would mean inventing a surface, which is worse than the debt. Reported as low-priority finding W41-F4 (cleanup) in build_log/WAVE41_REPORT.md so that "allowlisted" does not come to mean "forgotten".

GATE LIMITATION, PROVED HARMLESS BY READING THE SOURCE — every panel here has a trigger. The finding is "TabsContent value is not a string literal, so its trigger cannot be verified", which is an honest statement about static analysis, not about the page. The panel is generated by a map at client/src/pages/admin/Investors.tsx:855-856: `(["all", "investors", "founders", "consortium_partners"] as const).map((tab) => <TabsContent key={tab} value={tab}>`. The four values are a literal, closed, `as const` array, and each has a matching literal trigger in the same TabsList — verified individually: value="all" at :841, value="investors" at :844, value="founders" at :847, value="consortium_partners" at :850. Four panels, four triggers, identical spellings. The R2 rule (a panel with no trigger is dead UI) is therefore satisfied; only the gate's literal-value requirement is not. Deliberately allowlisted rather than "fixed" by unrolling the map into four copy-pasted panels, which would trade real duplication for a static-analysis convenience and create four places for a future change to be forgotten in three of.

STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO ORPHAN — the panel's value IS the Tabs' selected value. client/src/pages/collective/LeaderboardPage.tsx:127 renders <Tabs value={period} onValueChange={(v) => setPeriod(v as Period)}> and :134 renders a SINGLE <TabsContent value={period}>. The panel therefore always equals whatever the user has selected, so it can never be a panel the user cannot reach — it is the only panel and it follows the selection. The three triggers are literal and present at :129-131 (weekly, monthly, all-time), so every reachable selection has content. This is the standard shape for a tab strip that swaps one dataset rather than several layouts. Gate limitation only; no defect. Unrolling it into three identical panels differing solely in `value` would triple the markup to satisfy the analyser.

CANNOT HIDE AN ORPHANED PANEL, BECAUSE THIS FILE CONTAINS NO PANELS AT ALL. The unresolved trigger is client/src/pages/founder/CapTable.tsx:637, `<TabsTrigger value={v}>` inside `(Object.keys(VIEW_BLURBS) as View[]).map(...)` — a computed value, which the gate correctly declines to guess at. The reason this is provably safe rather than merely probably safe is the import list: line 7 imports { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger } and NOT TabsContent, and `grep -n TabsContent client/src/pages/founder/CapTable.tsx` returns nothing. This Tabs is a segmented CONTROL — selecting a view sets `view` state that re-renders the table below through ordinary conditional rendering, with no Radix panel involved. R2 exists to catch a panel with no trigger. With zero panels in the file, an unresolved trigger cannot orphan one, whatever `v` turns out to be. The triggers also carry stable literal testids (tab-fd / tab-ac / tab-basic) derived in the same expression, so they remain addressable by tests.

DELIBERATE ANCHOR-WRAPS-BUTTON IDIOM, and NOT repairable in Wave 41 without splitting one pattern in two. The anchor is a `download` link to /api/admin/contacts/sample-csv (InvestorImport.tsx:278) — a browser download must be an anchor; a <button> cannot express `download`. In every one of these sites the OUTER <a> is the real navigator and carries the destination — an external website, a mailto:, or a `download` link to a server PDF/CSV endpoint — while the <Button> is a visual skin with no onClick of its own (PartnerBilling is the one exception: its anchor carries the onClick that mints the checkout, and the Button is still only a skin). So nothing is unreachable and no behaviour is wrong: the click target the user sees navigates to the href on the anchor. What R3 is right about is that <button> inside <a> is invalid HTML, and this repo already contains the correct form — client/src/pages/CompanyDetails.tsx:572 uses <Button ... asChild> for exactly this job. It is NOT fixed here for a specific reason rather than convenience: one member of this pattern is client/src/pages/founder/Billing.tsx, which is SACRED (read, never edit) and whose modification needs a waiver ratified at all three enforcement points. Converting the other sites while Billing.tsx keeps the old shape would leave two idioms for one intent and would make the remaining violation look like an oversight instead of a constraint. Tracked as finding W41-F3 in build_log/WAVE41_REPORT.md for a single coordinated wave that carries the waiver. Allowlisted as a known, named, dated a11y/validity debt with a stated owner decision pending — not as a claim that it is correct.

DELIBERATE NESTING WITH AN EXPLICIT, IN-CODE ISOLATION — the stopPropagation is the evidence of intent. client/src/pages/founder/RoundNew.tsx:1009 renders each instrument choice as a selectable card: div role="button" tabIndex={0} aria-pressed={selected}, with both onClick and an Enter/Space onKeyDown, i.e. a correctly keyboard-operable custom radio. Inside it, :1036 renders <LearnMore>, which contains its own control. The nesting is not accidental and not unhandled: the LearnMore is wrapped in `<div onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}>` at :1035, precisely so that expanding the explanation does not also select the instrument. A developer who had not considered the interaction would not have written that line. Behaviourally both actions work and neither steals the other's click, and the pattern is the right product call — a founder choosing between SAFE / priced round / convertible needs the explanation AT the choice, not on another screen. The residual issue R3 names is real but narrower than the rule's headline: nested interactive content inside role="button" is awkward for screen readers. Recorded as finding W41-F5. NOT restructured in this wave because RoundNew's instrument selector is round-creation UI outside Wave 41's scope, and changing it blind is how a working flow gets broken to satisfy a linter.
